title: Unusual High-Frequency Verbs
lede: Learn the essential mini-paradigms and spelling changes of رَأَى، جَاءَ، أَتَى، أَخَذَ، أَعْطَى and other high-frequency unusual verbs.
nav: Hollow, Doubled and Weak Verb Patterns

items.feedback: رَأَى changes to رَأَيْـ before the suffix.
The high-frequency present form is يَرَى.
جَاءَ changes to جِئْـ before ـتُ.

options: Memorise high-frequency unusual verbs as complete mini-paradigms.
items.feedback: Small, repeated paradigms build reliable control.
Hollow-like short past stem before ـتُ.

options: force every verb into one pattern

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نَحْفَظُ بَعْضَ الْأَفْعَالِ كَعَائِلَاتٍ؟
Some extremely common verbs preserve old or irregular-looking changes. Accurate use comes from understanding what can be explained and retrieving what must be learned.
### Core
Use core forms of رَأَى، جَاءَ، أَخَذَ and أَعْطَى.
### Develop
Move the same verb across persons and time frames.
### Stretch
Compare alternative verbs such as جَاءَ / أَتَى and analyse orthographic changes.
[callout] Communication target: Use unusual verbs naturally in descriptions, plans and narratives.
## Diagnostic start
Check the forms you already recognise.
## The verb رَأَى / يَرَى
This essential verb shifts visibly between past and present and preserves a written hamza in several past forms.

TABLE: Function | رَأَى / يَرَى | Model // past he | رَأَى | رَأَى الْفِيلْمَ. // past she | رَأَتْ | رَأَتْ صَدِيقَتَهَا. // past I/we | رَأَيْتُ / رَأَيْنَا | رَأَيْنَا الْبَحْرَ. // present I/he/we | أَرَى / يَرَى / نَرَى | نَرَى الْجَبَلَ. // future | سَأَرَى | سَأَرَى النَّتِيجَةَ غَدًا.
[callout] Spelling alert: Keep the hamza in رَأَيْتُ . The present يَرَى is a high-frequency irregular form best learned whole.
## Coming: جَاءَ / يَجِيءُ and أَتَى / يَأْتِي
Hamza placement and stem changes make these forms worth deliberate retrieval.

TABLE: Function | جَاءَ / يَجِيءُ | Alternative high-frequency pair // past he/she | جَاءَ / جَاءَتْ | أَتَى / أَتَتْ // past I/we | جِئْتُ / جِئْنَا | أَتَيْتُ / أَتَيْنَا // present I/he | أَجِيءُ / يَجِيءُ | آتِي / يَأْتِي // present we/they | نَجِيءُ / يَجِيئُونَ | نَأْتِي / يَأْتُونَ
[callout] House approach: Learn both جَاءَ / يَجِيءُ and the very common أَتَى / يَأْتِي . Use one consistently within a sentence rather than mixing stems.
## Other high-frequency unusual verbs
These verbs appear constantly in everyday communication and deserve compact reference families.

TABLE: Verb family | Key forms | Meaning // أَخَذَ / يَأْخُذُ | أَخَذْتُ، آخُذُ، خُذْ | take // أَكَلَ / يَأْكُلُ | أَكَلْتُ، آكُلُ، كُلْ | eat // أَعْطَى / يُعْطِي | أَعْطَيْتُ، أُعْطِي، أَعْطِ | give // بَقِيَ / يَبْقَى | بَقِيتُ، أَبْقَى | remain // أَرَادَ / يُرِيدُ | أَرَدْتُ، أُرِيدُ | want
[callout/warning] First-person hamza: آخُذُ and آكُلُ are not written with two separate hamzas. The madda represents the contraction.
## Memorise intelligently
Small paradigms and recurring sentence frames are more durable than long unconnected lists.
### Mini-paradigm method
Say five forms in one rhythm:
رَأَى — رَأَتْ — رَأَيْتُ — يَرَى — أَرَى
### Sentence-frame method
Change the time expression and object, not only the isolated verb.
### Contrast similar meanings
جَاءَ / أَتَى، يَجِيءُ / يَأْتِي
Recognise both; choose one accurately for production.
### Orthography audit
Check hamza, madda, alif maqṣūra and suffix attachment.
## Unusual-verb spelling clinic
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
### Seeing
✗ أَنَا رَيْتُ الْمُبَارَاةَ
✓ أَنَا رَأَيْتُ الْمُبَارَاةَ
Keep the hamza and the full رَأَيْـ stem.
### Coming
✗ أَنَا جَاءْتُ مُبَكِّرًا
✓ أَنَا جِئْتُ مُبَكِّرًا
The first-person past is جِئْتُ.
### Taking
✗ أَنَا أَأْخُذُ الْحَافِلَةَ
✓ أَنَا آخُذُ الْحَافِلَةَ
Use madda in the first-person present.
### Wanting
✗ أَنَا أَرَادْتُ أَنْ أَدْرُسَ
✓ أَنَا أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَدْرُسَ
The hollow stem shortens before ـتُ.
## Replayable retrieval game
Strengthen accurate high-frequency forms.
## Apply the grammar across skills
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
### 📖 Reading workshop
Read a personal message containing رأى، جاء، أخذ، أعطى and أراد. Identify the subject and time of each form, then infer any unfamiliar form from context.
### 🎧 Listening workshop
Listen to a short account and distinguish جِئْتُ, جَاءَتْ, جَاءُوا, أَجِيءُ and يَجِيئُونَ.
### 🗣️ Speaking workshop
Answer “What did you see?”, “How did you come?”, “What did you take?” and “What do you want to do next?” in connected Arabic.
### 🛠️ Editing workshop
Correct a message with misplaced hamzas, a missing madda and three wrong stem choices.
### ✍️ Integrated production task
Write a 100–120-word description of an event you attended or saw. Use at least five unusual high-frequency verbs across two or three time frames.
[callout] Model: أَمْسِ جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مُبَكِّرًا، وَرَأَيْتُ مَعْرِضًا جَمِيلًا. أَخَذْتُ بَعْضَ الصُّوَرِ، وَأَعْطَيْتُ صَدِيقَتِي نُسْخَةً مِنْهَا.
[callout] Success checklist: Include forms from رأى، جاء/أتى، أخذ، أعطى and أراد; check every hamza and weak ending.
Save and mark complete Clear
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Create a margin checklist for hamza, madda, alif maqṣūra and subject agreement.
## Final mastery check
Retrieve the mini-paradigms accurately.
### Lesson mastery summary
- use رَأَى / يَرَى across common persons and time frames;
- use جَاءَ / يَجِيءُ and recognise أَتَى / يَأْتِي;
- spell high-frequency hamza and madda forms accurately;
- retrieve unusual verbs inside meaningful sentences.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
